confirmed.location: page1.body, 4th paragraph, sentence 1 ("Every real transfer scatters some energy into low, useless warmth.")
confirmed.issue: "low, useless warmth" is an unnatural collocation. In English, "low" cannot premodify "warmth" to mean "low-grade/low-quality." The established technical term is "low-grade heat" (저급 에너지/폐열). As written, "low warmth" reads either as a temperature reading (which contradicts the point — the issue is energy quality, not temperature magnitude) or simply as an error.

confirmed.suggestion: "Every real transfer scatters some energy into low-grade, useless warmth." (or "...into diffuse, useless warmth"). The Korean translation [17] "낮고 쓸모없는 온기" should be revised in parallel to "저급하고 쓸모없는 열" — "낮은 온기" is equally unnatural in Korean.

2) 내부 불일치 — 같은 문장을 인용하는 page4.vocab 두 곳이 모두 "low"를 조용히 삭제한다. line 481 "scatter": "Every real transfer scatters some energy as heat." / line 426 "transfer": "Every real transfer scatters some energy into useless warmth." 지적자가 든 교차검증 1건보다 실제로는 2건으로 더 강하며, 집필 측도 이 수식어를 유지하지 못했다는 신호다.

minors.location: page1.body, 1st paragraph ("The motion of your hands does not vanish. It simply turns into heat.")
minors.issue: Strictly, it is the *kinetic energy* of the hands (via friction), not "the motion," that is converted to heat — motion itself is not a conserved quantity. The paragraph's own thesis is about *energy* conservation, so the referent slips. This is a standard pedagogical simplification and readable at this level, but it sits awkwardly right before the formal definition "energy is never created or destroyed."
minors.evidence: "The motion of your hands does not vanish. It simply turns into heat. Physicists describe this exchange with one strict rule called the conservation of energy..."
minors.suggestion: "The energy of your moving hands does not vanish. It simply turns into heat." — one word change that makes the bridge to the conservation rule exact.

minors.location: page1.body, 3rd paragraph, sentence 1 ("Yet this flow obeys a strict one-way sign.")
minors.issue: Mixed metaphor / imprecise noun. A flow obeys a *rule* or a *law*; a driver obeys a *sign*. "one-way sign" is a traffic image that has not been set up anywhere in the passage, and it clashes with "one strict rule" in paragraph 1 which used the literal register.
minors.evidence: "Yet this flow obeys a strict one-way sign." (Translation [13] "엄격한 일방통행 표지판을 따른다" reproduces the same oddity.)
minors.suggestion: "Yet this flow obeys a strict one-way rule." If the traffic image is wanted, make it explicit: "Yet this flow follows a strict one-way street."
